title: Who Keeps Our Stock Market Running Smoothly? Understanding Market Makers
description: Market Makers are financial firms or individuals who continuously offer to buy and sell specific shares. They ensure there's always someone willing to trade, .

faq.q: Who can be a Market Maker in India?
faq.a: In India, typically, financial institutions like brokerage firms, banks, or dedicated trading firms with sufficient capital and technological infrastructure can be approved as Market Makers by the stock exchanges and SEBI.

faq.q: Do Market Makers only deal with large investors?
faq.a: No, Market Makers provide liquidity for all participants in the market, including individual retail investors like you, as well as large institutional investors. Their presence ensures that any size order can be executed smoothly.

faq.q: How do Market Makers get their inventory of shares?
faq.a: Market Makers build their inventory by buying shares from sellers in the market. They continuously adjust their bid and ask prices to manage this inventory, ensuring they have enough shares to sell when there's demand and can buy when there's supply.

faq.q: What happens if there are no Market Makers?
faq.a: Without Market Makers, the market would be much less liquid. It would be harder and slower to buy or sell shares, and you might have to accept much wider price differences (larger spreads) to execute your trades. Prices could also become much more volatile.

faq.q: Are Market Makers involved in all types of securities?
faq.a: Market Makers are most commonly associated with actively traded stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and derivatives (like futures and options). Their role is particularly crucial in segments where liquidity might otherwise be low.
